questions.question: A and B undertake to do a piece of work for Rs. 18,750. A can do it in 20 days and B can do it in 30 days. With the help of C, they finished it in 8 days. How much C should be paid for his work in proportion?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of **A**, **B**, and **(A+B+C)** = 1/20 : 1/30 : 1/8

Multiply by LCM(20, 30, 8) = 120 → **A : B : (A+B+C)** = 6 : 4 : 15

Efficiency of **C** = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units

**C's wage share** = (Efficiency of C / Total Efficiency) × Total Amount

**C's share** = (5/15) × 18,750 = 1/3 × 18,750 = ₹6,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,250.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 20 days

Time taken by **B** = 30 days

Time taken by **A, B, and C** together = 8 days

Total wage amount = ₹18,750

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Wage Share = (Individual Efficiency ÷ Total Efficiency) × Total Wage

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 20

 120 ÷ 20 = 6
 
 

 B
 30
 120 ÷ 30 = 4
 
 

 A + B + C
 8
 120 ÷ 8 = 15
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **A + B + C** = 15 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = Efficiency of (A+B+C) − Efficiency of (A+B)

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units/day

⇒ Ratio of wages (A : B : C) = 6 : 4 : 5

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 6 + 4 + 5 = 15

⇒ **C's share** = (5 ÷ 15) × 18,750

⇒ **C's share** = 1/3 × 18,750 = ₹6,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,250.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Principle

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the **work done** by each individual. If they work for the same amount of time, the wage ratio is equal to their **efficiency ratio**.

Combined Efficiency

Total efficiency of a group working together is the **sum of individual efficiencies**: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ.

Time-Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a task (Efficiency ∝ 1/Time) when work is constant.

questions.question:
PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in a circle with centre O. ∠PQR and ∠PSR are in the ratio

11 ∶ 7. If PQ = QR, then find. ∠OPQ
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. Let ∠PQR = 11x and ∠PSR = 7x.

11x + 7x = 180° ⇒ 18x = 180° ⇒ x = 10°. So, ∠PQR = 110° and ∠PSR = 70°.

In isosceles ΔPQR (PQ = QR): ∠QPR = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°.

Central angle ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR = 2 × 70° = 140°.

In isosceles ΔOPR (OP = OR): ∠OPR = (180° − 140°) ÷ 2 = 20°.

∠OPQ = ∠QPR + ∠OPR = 35° + 20° = 55°.

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Cyclic quadrilateral** PQRS with center O. Ratio ∠PQR : ∠PSR = 11 : 7. Side **PQ = QR**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Sum of **opposite angles** of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

2. Angle subtended by an arc at the center is **double** the angle subtended at the circumference.

3. In an **isosceles triangle**, angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1cae76ef0d456263dc1fe46e8e6d13d7cb310b6fe3b57cf8e42488323013f700.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180° (Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral)

⇒ 11k + 7k = 180° ⇒ 18k = 180° ⇒ k = 10°

⇒ ∠PQR = 110° and ∠PSR = 70°

⇒ In ΔPQR, PQ = QR ⇒ ∠QPR = ∠QRP

⇒ ∠QPR = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR = 2 × 70° = 140° (Angle at center property)

⇒ In ΔOPR, OP = OR (radii) ⇒ ∠OPR = ∠ORP

⇒ ∠OPR = (180° − 140°) ÷ 2 = 20°

⇒ Since ∠PQR > 90°, center O and vertex Q lie on opposite sides of chord PR.

⇒ ∠OPQ = ∠QPR + ∠OPR = 35° + 20° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorems

The sum of opposite angles is 180°. The exterior angle is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Angle Subtended by a Chord

A chord subtends an angle at the center that is twice the angle it subtends at the major arc of the circumference.

Isosceles Property in Circles

Triangles formed by the center and any two points on the circumference (radii) are always isosceles.</p

questions.question: One-eighth of a number is 12 less than half of 42. Find one-fourth of the number.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

One-eighth of a number is 12 less than half of 42

**Calculation:**

Let the number be 8a

According to the question,

42 × 1/2 - 8a × 1/8 = 12

⇒ 21 - a = 12

⇒ a = 9

So, the number is 9 × 8 = 72

Now, 1/4th of the number = 72 × 1/4 = 18

**∴ Required answer is 18**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 7800 amounts to Rs. 10381.80 at *x*% p.a. in 2 years when the interest is compounded 8-monthly. What will be the compound interest on the same sum at (*x* + 5)% p.a. in one year, if the interest is compounded half yearly?

For n = 3, 1 + r = ³√1.331 = 1.1 ⇒ 8-monthly rate (r) = 10%.

Annual rate **x** = 10% × (12 / 8) = 15%. New annual rate = 15% + 5% = **20%**.

Compounded **half-yearly** for 1 year (2 periods): Rate = 10% per period.

Effective interest rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10 / 100) = 21%.

**Compound Interest** = 21% of 7800 = 78 × 21 = ₹1638.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1638.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c2a0e123a19366692c93ee1091f90c10a8bde54673b925c0223c141e851c468.png]

⇒ r/100 = 0.1 ⇒ r = 10% (Rate for 8 months).

⇒ Annual rate x = (10 / 8) × 12 = 15% p.a.

⇒ New rate = x + 5 = 15 + 5 = 20% p.a.

⇒ For **half-yearly compounding**: New r = 20 / 2 = 10%; n = 1 × 2 = 2.

⇒ CI = 7800 [(1 + 10/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 7800 [1.21 − 1] = 7800 × 0.21 = ₹1638.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1638.**

Sum of circle areas = (22/7) × (6² + 4² + 2²) = (22/7) × 56 = 176 cm².

Area of square = 576 − 176 = 400 cm².

Side of square = √400 = 20 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

**Area of Circle** = π × r²

**Area of Square** = side²

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (36 + 16 + 4) = (22/7) × 56

⇒ Area = 22 × 8 = 176 cm²

⇒ **Remaining Area** = Sheet Area − Total Circle Area

questions.question: A certain sum is invested on compound interest at 18% per annum for 1 year 4 months, the interest being compounded 8-monthly. If the compound interest is Rs. 3,816, then find the sum (in Rs.).

From the top of the tower of 30 m height, a man is observing a kid playing on the ground at an angle of depression of 30 degrees. Find the distance between the foot of the tower and the kid.

(Height of man and kid are to be ignored for calculation)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°-60°-90° triangle**, the sides opposite to these angles are in the ratio **1 : √3 : 2**.

The **height** of the tower is opposite the **30° angle**, so 1 unit = **30 m**.

The **distance** from the foot is opposite the **60° angle**, so √3 units = **30 × √3 m**.

Distance = **30√3 m**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30√3 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height of tower (AB)** = 30 m

**Angle of depression** = 30°

**Angle of elevation (θ)** = 30° (Alternate interior angles are equal)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f2300330c7686ed0f499e2267ec2d63e045fb7bb998d467a68e520e9fd713c5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = **Perpendicular / Base**

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan 30° = **AB / BC**

⇒ 1 / √3 = **30 / BC**

⇒ BC = **30 × √3**

⇒ BC = **30√3 m**

**∴ The correct answer is 30√3 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression and Elevation

The **Angle of Depression** from an observer's eye to an object below is numerically equal to the **Angle of Elevation** from the object to the observer's eye because they are **alternate interior angles**.

Trigonometric Ratios

questions.question: Avra travels from A to B at 74 km/h and returns from B to A through the same route at 111 km/h. What was his average speed during the two-way journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** for both journeys is the same, the **Average Speed** is the **Harmonic Mean** of the two speeds.

Formula: **Average Speed** = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Here, x = 74 km/h and y = 111 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 74 × 111) ÷ (74 + 111) = 16428 ÷ 185

Average Speed = 88.8 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 88.8 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 74 km/h

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 111 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59c738b0949efdb718258bb89f88ad10ead760643114cf61ce7eaf2ce682f4d6.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between A and B be the LCM of 74 and 111, which is 222 km.

⇒ Time taken from A to B (T₁) = 222 ÷ 74 = 3 hours.

⇒ Time taken from B to A (T₂) = 222 ÷ 111 = 2 hours.

⇒ Total Distance = 222 + 222 = 444 km.

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 2 = 5 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 444 ÷ 5 = 88.8 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 88.8 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

If a person covers distances d₁, d₂, d₃ at speeds s₁, s₂, s₃, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂ + d₃/s₃).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Constant Time Scenario

If a person travels at speed x for time t and speed y for the same time t, the Average Speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (x + y) ÷ 2.</p

r = radius

questions.question: Renu's marks were wrongly entered as 99 in place of 9. Due to this error, the average marks of the class were 2.25 more than the actual average. What is the number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net increase in total marks = 99 − 9 = 90

Increase in class average = 2.25

Number of students = Net increase in total marks ÷ Increase in average

⇒ Number of students = 90 ÷ 2.25 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual marks of Renu = 9

Wrongly entered marks = 99

Increase in average marks of the class = 2.25

 
 Number of Students (N) = Total Error ÷ Avg Increase
 
 
 
 Total Error = 99 − 9 = +90 Marks
 
 
 
•

 +2.25
 . . .
 +2.25

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

Let the total number of students in the class be n and the correct sum of marks of all students be S.

⇒ Correct Average = S ÷ n

⇒ Incorrect Sum of marks = S − 9 + 99 = S + 90

⇒ Incorrect Average = (S + 90) ÷ n = (S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)

We know that: Incorrect Average − Correct Average = 2.25

⇒ [(S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)] − (S ÷ n) = 2.25

⇒ 90 ÷ n = 2.25

⇒ n = 90 ÷ 2.25

⇒ n = 9000 ÷ 225

⇒ n = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 students.**

When a value is replaced by a larger value, the net increase is distributed equally among all observations. Thus, Change in Average = Difference in values ÷ Total Number of observations.

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages A₁ and A₂, then the combined average is (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Change due to Addition

If a new observation is added and the average increases, the new value is greater than the initial average. New Value = Old Average + (Total new elements × Increase in Average).
